The guides

No. 01

What does an event planner cost in Australia?

Two of the most cited Australian sources disagree by thousands of dollars. This guide sets their figures side by side, explains why they differ, and shows what a planning fee looks like against a real budget.

No. 02

Planner, coordinator or stylist?

Three different jobs that get used as though they were one. Which one you ask for changes the brief, the quote and what turns up on the day.

No. 03

The run sheet, explained

What goes in a wedding run sheet or event run sheet, who it goes to, and the version control problem that ruins more days than bad weather does. On this page, below.

Run sheet

What is a run sheet, and what goes in one?

A run sheet is the single timed document that every supplier, the venue and your key people work from on the day. It is not the same as your planning timeline and it is not the same as a guest itinerary.

Of all the event planning tips worth acting on, this is the one that changes the most: write the run sheet properly. A wedding run sheet or event run sheet answers one question for every person working on your event: what am I doing, where, and at what time. Everything else is a distraction. The most common mistake is to write a beautiful schedule for the guests and never produce the operational one for the suppliers, which is the one that actually protects the day.

What every run sheet needs

  • Bump in. Who arrives when, through which entrance, and what they need to be let in with. Include the venue's earliest access time, because it is almost always earlier than people assume and sometimes much later.
  • Supplier contacts. Business name, the name of the person who will actually be there, and their mobile. Not the office number.
  • Timed running order. Every element with a start time and a duration: ceremony, arrivals, canapes, seating, entree, speeches, cake, first dance, last drinks.
  • Who cues what. Speeches and formalities go wrong when nobody has been told they are responsible for starting them. Name a person against every cue.
  • Meal and break times for suppliers. Photographers, musicians and coordinators working an eight hour day need a fed break, and the caterer needs to know when.
  • Pack down. What leaves that night, what leaves the next morning, who is collecting it and who has the key.
  • Wet weather and heat calls. The alternative plan, and the specific time by which the call has to be made. A wet weather plan with no decision deadline is not a plan.

The version control problem

Most run sheet failures are not content failures. They are version failures. Four suppliers turn up working from three different documents because the ceremony moved by fifteen minutes in week ten and only two of them were told. Fix it by naming one owner of the document, putting a version date in the header, and sending the final version to everyone at the same time in the final week. If you have booked on-the-day coordination, this is precisely the job you are paying for.

How far ahead to write it

Draft it at eight weeks and finalise it at two. Earlier than eight weeks and too much is still moving. Later than two and you lose the chance to catch the conflicts, which is the entire point of writing it down.

Checklist

What an event planning checklist should actually contain

Most published checklists are lists of things to buy. A working one is a list of decisions in the order that keeps your later options open.

A decision-order checklist for an Australian event. Adjust the months for a shorter lead time, but keep the order.
WhenThe decisionWhy it comes here
FirstBudget range and guest countEverything downstream is priced per head or constrained by the room. Deciding these last is the most expensive mistake people make.
NextDate, or a shortlist of datesSuppliers and venues are booked by date. A firm date makes every following conversation shorter.
ThenVenueThe venue sets your capacity, your catering options, your bump in window and often your supplier list. It constrains more than anything else you choose.
ThenThe suppliers who take one booking a dayPhotographer, celebrant, band. These book out first for peak Saturdays.
ThenCatering and drinksUsually priced per head, so it needs the guest count locked.
ThenStyling, florals, hire and cakeThese can adapt to what is already booked. Doing them earlier means redoing them.
8 weeks outRun sheet drafted, final numbers requestedLate enough to be real, early enough to fix conflicts.
2 weeks outRun sheet finalised and circulated, final payments scheduledThe last point at which a change is easy for everyone.

Scroll the table sideways to see every column.

If you are working to a shorter timeline, the order matters more, not less. Skipping straight to styling before the guest count is settled is how people end up rebuying things.

Brief

What to put in an event brief before you ask for quotes

A planner cannot quote against a feeling. Six lines of writing will get you a far more useful answer than a long phone call.

The occasion and the date

Or an approximate month. Say if the date is movable, because it changes what a planner can offer you.

Where, roughly

Suburb or region is enough. Venue name if you have one. Planners price travel, so location changes the number.

Guest count, even a range

Under 30, 60 to 100, over 150. Almost every cost on an event is a function of this.

A budget range you can defend

Not a final figure. A range, plus which parts you would protect if it tightened.

See the cost guide

The level of help you want

Full planning, partial planning or on-the-day coordination. If you are not sure, say so.

Compare the levels

Your three non-negotiables

The things that have to happen for the day to feel like yours. A good planner will work around almost anything else.

Straight answers

Questions about planning your own event

What is the difference between a run sheet and a timeline?

A planning timeline covers the months before the event and lists decisions. A run sheet covers the day itself and lists timed actions with a named person against each one. You need both, and they are not interchangeable. The run sheet is the one your suppliers work from.

When should I write the run sheet?

Draft it about eight weeks out and finalise it about two weeks out. Earlier and too much is still changing. Later and you lose the window to catch conflicts between suppliers, which is the main reason the document exists.

Do I need an event planning checklist if I have hired a planner?

Your planner will run their own. A short personal checklist is still useful for the decisions only you can make, such as the guest list, the speeches and the things you want protected if the budget tightens.

What is an event brief template?

An event brief is a short written summary of the occasion, date, location, guest count, budget range and level of help you want, sent to planners before they quote. The six items listed above are the working template. Anything longer tends to go unread.

Are these guides written for Australian events?

Yes. Timings, seasons, supplier conventions and pricing sources are all Australian. Peak wedding months in most of the country are March, April, October and November, which is why Saturdays in those months book out first.
